Après son Gala de lancement du mois d’Avril, la 2e Édition de l’Institut Djibouti Espace de Réflexion et d’Echanges (DERE) en partenariat avec la BCIMR et Djibouti Telecom s’est organisée le mercredi 20 Décembre 2023 au Sheraton Hôtel avec pour objet de mouvoir les perspectives de l’an 2024-2025 de DERE, ouvrant la voie à de nouveaux défis au service du développement de notre pays.
DERE est une organisation indépendante, solidaire et formatrice, fondée sur le principe de neutralité et d’impartialité pour mieux refléter l’interface et l’espace qu’elle présente.
Pour cette réception de prestige, l’Institut DERE a réuni dans sa tendance structurelle plus de 30 personnes dont la plupart sont des membres d’honneur. Ont chaleureusement pris part à cette conférence, Mme Sylvie Tabesse, ambassadrice de l’Union Européenne, Mme la Cheffe de coopération de l’Union Européenne, Mme Fatou FALL Représentante de la Banque Mondiale à Djibouti, Mme Nancy OSTROWSKI la Représentante adjointe de l’USAID, l’Attaché de Coopération de l’Ambassade de France, Mr l’Ambassadeur Guelleh Idriss Omar, la Directrice adjointe Grande Entreprise BCIMR, Mme Hibo Mahamoud, directrice de D-Money, le directeur Commercial de DMP, Mr Kenedid Ibrahim Président de l’Union Presse Francophone, Mr Said Del Waiss Président de HALT Group, représentantes de la Chambre de Commerce et du FSD (Fonds Saoudien de Djibouti) ainsi que la présence de plusieurs honorables invités et les membres du Conseil Administratif et de la Direction du DERE.
Cette conférence de réflexion stratégique de DERE est animée avec brio par son Directeur General M. Mahamoud Ahmed Sougueh avec la corroboration de la présidente du conseil d’administration du DERE Mme Sarah Houssein Ahmed, qui ouvre les festivités en déclarant : « C’est toujours un plaisir pour moi de vous accueillir au nom de toute l’équipe de DERE, votre présence parmi nous nous ravit et nous réconforte dans la suite de nos actions. Nous sommes réunis en ce jour pour faire le point des perspectives de DERE, lancée en avril 2023 comme institut de type « think tank » pour contribuer à l’élaboration des politiques publiques et à la croissance économique du pays. L’institut DERE se veut être un projet de société, de rayonnement de la culture, du dialogue, du partage d’expériences et d’expertise. Notre politique est de devenir un partenaire privilégié aussi bien pour les décideurs politiques que les opérateurs privés et partenaires de développement.
Pour ce faire, l’Institut a cependant besoin de votre soutien pour réaliser ses ambitions, un soutien moral comme votre présence et participation, un soutien technique comme l’expertise et surtout un soutien financier, vu que sans ressources financières, une organisation ne peut se développer et se professionnaliser.
Nous remercions tous les sponsors et partenaires gouvernementaux, privés et de coopération internationale qui nous ont accompagné depuis le début. Je vous remercie ».
Puis, c’est au tour du DG de DERE M. Mahamoud Ahmed Sougueh de nous relater la teneur et le pourquoi de cette journée dans cette espace de réflexion et de collaboration, il déclare : « C’est un réel plaisir pour moi et mon équipe de vous accueillir, un moment qui revêt une importance particulière pour notre Institut.
Avant de vous présenter nos perspectives 2024-2025, permettez-moi de vous dire que ces quatre petites lettres DERE ont une signification profonde pour nous. Nous avons franchi plusieurs étapes avant d’être capable et d’oser se présenter devant des acteurs tels que vous pour discuter de programmes et projets. Depuis 2019, DERE organise des débats d’idées impliquant les décideurs politiques, économiques, sociaux, culturels et universitaires, en interaction avec les citoyens. Nous sommes conscients du chantier de l’ampleur du chantier. Nous visons positivement à influencer les politiques publiques, à instaurer des espaces de réflexion, de partage et d’influences entre les citoyens et le gouvernement. Notre objectif est de promouvoir la participation active des jeunes et les femmes à travers les programmes PJAA (Programme des Jeunes Acteurs et Actrices) et PLF (Programme Leadership Féminin), des programmes qui visent à autonomiser les jeunes en tant qu’acteurs de leur insertion économique, sociale et culturelle, de renforcer en s’alignant sur la politique nationale du Genre l’institutionnalisation de la voix féminine par le biais du développement de Leadership féminin ».
Enfin la plus grande richesse de DERE vient de la contribution des participants. Au fur et à mesure qu’ils se rencontrent et qu’ils apprennent à se connaître, ils développent une atmosphère de confiance et se sentent libres de partager leurs pensées et leurs sentiments. L’Institut DERE vise à apporter dans ses programmes des progrès aux efforts du gouvernement en matière de diversification de l’économie et de la réduction de la pauvreté.
Saleh Ibrahim Rayaleh

DERE is an independent, solidarity-based and training organisation, founded on the principle of neutrality and impartiality the better to reflect the interface and the space that it represents.

Then it was the turn of DERE's Director General Mr Mahamoud Ahmed Sougueh to recount to us the substance and the rationale of this day in this space of reflection and collaboration; he declared: "It is a real pleasure for me and my team to welcome you, a moment of particular importance for our Institute.

Before presenting our 2024-2025 outlook to you, allow me to tell you that these four small letters DERE have a deep meaning for us. Our objective is to promote the active participation of young people and women through the PJAA (Programme for Young Actors) and PLF (Female Leadership Programme) programmes, programmes that aim to empower young people as actors of their economic, social and cultural integration, and to strengthen, in line with the national Gender policy, the institutionalisation of the female voice through the development of female leadership."

The DERE Institute aims to bring, through its programmes, progress to the government's efforts in diversifying the economy and reducing poverty.

The US government has officially terminated 83 per cent of the programmes run by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).
It has also cancelled 5,200 contracts initially awarded by the agency to several organisations.
This development comes several weeks after the suspension of all foreign assistance and the issuance of a stop-work order on the agency.
In a post on X on Monday, the country’s Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, announced that the US Department of State, along with Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), made this decision after a six-week review of the agency’s activities.
“The 5,200 contracts that are now cancelled spent tens of billions of dollars in ways that did not serve, (and in some cases even harmed), the core national interests of the United States,” he said.
“In consultation with Congress, we intend for the remaining 18% of programmes we are keeping (approximately 1,000) to be administered more effectively under the State Department,” MrRubio further wrote.
Suspension of USAID programmes
Due to the drastic elimination of numerous USAID programmes, many international projects dedicated to health, education, and humanitarian relief worldwide that were initially suspended will now end.
The suspension of foreign assistance raised global concerns and alarmed many African developing countries, which depended heavily on US foreign aid.
In Nigeria, clinics and research centres shut down following President Donald Trump’s executive order on January 20.
PREMIUM TIMES also reported that intervention programmes were abruptly suspended, community health workers lost their jobs, and USAID health workers deployed to hard-to-reach areas were recalled.
Additionally, humanitarian aid dwindled, leaving vulnerable groups without essential support. Many had hoped the aid freeze and stop-work order would be lifted after 90 days.
However, Mr Rubio’s recent announcement confirms the ultimate elimination of several USAID-funded programmes.
Nigeria govt’s effort
Meanwhile, the Nigerian government has begun working to bridge the funding gap created by the new US policies.
The National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA) earlier announced its plan to strengthen its domestic HIV response and produce HIV-related medical tools, including test kits and antiretroviral drugs.
On 3 February, the Federal Executive Council (FEC) approved $1.07 billion to finance the healthcare sector reforms under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE) programme.
PREMIUM TIMES reported that Wale Edun, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, disclosed that FEC also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment.
As part of government efforts to address the funding gap, the Nigerian Senate also recently allocated an additional N300 billion to the health sector in the 2025 budget.
The additional allocation, equivalent to $200 million, will target health programmes such as Tuberculosis, HIV, Malaria and Polio.

En prélude au Salon des Petites et moyennes entreprises qui se tiendra du 25 au 27 novembre prochain, le ministre de l’Emploi des Jeunes et de la promotion des Petites et moyennes Entreprises, Nadine Dako Tamadaho a animé hier jeudi 22 octobre à Cotonou un déjeuner de presse. C’était pour expliquer aux hommes des médias le bien fondé et les avantages de cette manifestation.
Depuis trois années, le ministère en charge des Petites et moyennes Entreprises organise un Salon des Petites et moyennes entreprises et un marché des produits et services locaux.
Après deux éditions, une évaluation a été faite par les organisateurs qui ont conclu que le bilan est mitigé. 
Ainsi, l’Agence nationale pour la promotion de l’emploi a décidé d’organiser au cours de cette année 2015, un salon des Petites et moyennes Entreprises, en l’élargissant au marché des produits et services locaux.
Le ministre de l’Emploi des Jeunes et de la promotion des Petites et moyennes Entreprises, Nadine Dako a indiqué que la rencontre avec les journalistes vise à annoncer les couleurs de l’évènement qui aura lieu en novembre prochain.
L’apport des institutions, a-t-elle insisté, est important pour la survie des entreprises. «Aujourd’hui, il y a plus de 8 800 entreprises qui se sont créées, mais malheureusement, il y en a beaucoup qui ne résistent pas», a poursuivi le ministre.
Le Salon des Petites et moyennes Entreprises sera placé sous le thème ; «Financement de la PME : Défis et perspectives». Un thème qui, selon Nadine Dako, est très important et nécessite que les institutions, les organismes d’accompagnement des Petites et moyennes entreprises, et les promoteurs se donnent la main pour la réussite des activités du secteur.
Appelé à regrouper des offreurs de services ou accompagnateurs des PME, le salon a pour objectif d’inciter la création des petites et moyennes entreprises, d'encourager celles qui existent déjà, d’inciter et encourager les opérateurs du secteur informel à se formaliser, de mettre en exergue les filières porteuses de croissance et de susciter la production et la consommation du made in Bénin.
La cible qui exposera, sera constituée des institutions bancaires, des structures de microfinance et des sociétés d’assurance, des bureaux d’études, des agences conseils, des cabinets d’expertise comptable ou d’audit, de l’administration publique, des organismes nationaux et internationaux tels que le CNCB, le PNUD, l’AFD, l’USAID.
Au cours de ce salon, des rencontres d’échanges à travers des formations, des conférences et ateliers avec des porteurs de projets, des étudiants ou des représentants de PME sur des sujets pertinents seront aussi organisés. Un créneau sera offert aux structures d’accompagnement des PME qui le souhaitent, pour exposer leur particularité en faveur des petites et moyennes entreprises.
L’innovation de cette année est qu’un documentaire sera réalisé au terme du salon, pour résumer en images et en son les principales activités et mettre en relief les acquis de l’évènement, puis donner la parole aux différents acteurs.

Ahead of the Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Fair, which will be held from 25 to 27 November, the Minister of Youth Employment and the Promotion of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises, Nadine Dako Tamadaho, hosted a press lunch yesterday, Thursday 22 October, in Cotonou. It was to explain to media professionals the rationale and the advantages of this event.
For three years now, the ministry in charge of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises has organised a Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Fair and a market of local products and services.
After two editions, an evaluation was carried out by the organisers, who concluded that the results were mixed.
Thus, the National Agency for the Promotion of Employment decided to organise, during this year 2015, a Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Fair, broadening it to include the market of local products and services.
The Minister of Youth Employment and the Promotion of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises, Nadine Dako, indicated that the meeting with journalists aims to set the tone for the event that will take place next November.
The contribution of institutions, she insisted, is important for the survival of businesses. "Today, more than 8,800 businesses have been created, but unfortunately many of them do not survive," the minister continued.
The Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Fair will be held under the theme "Financing SMEs: Challenges and Prospects". A theme which, according to Nadine Dako, is very important and requires that institutions, SME support organisations and promoters join hands for the success of the sector's activities.
Intended to bring together service providers and SME support organisations, the fair aims to encourage the creation of small and medium-sized enterprises, to encourage those that already exist, to prompt and encourage operators in the informal sector to formalise, to highlight growth-bearing value chains and to stimulate the production and consumption of goods made in Benin.
The target group that will exhibit will consist of banking institutions, microfinance bodies and insurance companies, consultancy firms, advisory agencies, accounting or audit practices, the public administration, and national and international organisations such as the CNCB, UNDP, AFD and USAID.
During this fair, exchange meetings through training sessions, conferences and workshops with project promoters, students or SME representatives on relevant topics will also be organised. A slot will be offered to SME support structures that wish to present what is distinctive about their offering for small and medium-sized enterprises.
This year's innovation is that a documentary will be produced at the end of the fair, to summarise in images and sound the main activities and highlight the gains of the event, and then give the floor to the various stakeholders.

By: Sarah Baafi
The Minister of Finance, Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, has reiterated the government’s focus on food security and economic stability during a meeting with Her Excellency Myriam Montrat, the Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana.
Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson described food security as a national priority, emphasizing the need for collaborative efforts to address rising food prices and their impact on vulnerable populations.
“More than one million Ghanaians are at risk of food insecurity due to skyrocketing prices,” he said, referencing alarming statistics from the World Food Programme.
He also highlighted the Goldbod initiative, describing it as a transformative project aimed at improving gold export tracking, stabilizing the cedi, increasing foreign exchange inflows, and creating jobs.
Acknowledging past challenges within Cocobod, he stated, “We cannot let isolated setbacks overshadow the invaluable contributions Cocobod has made to Ghana’s development or derail promising initiatives like Goldbod.”
He expressed confidence that Goldbod would soon be fully operational, delivering long-term stability and inclusive growth.
Mr Ato Forson reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program, noting that corrective actions had been taken to address structural slippages inherited from the previous administration.
“We are committed to ensuring fiscal discipline and achieving key economic targets under the IMF program,” he assured.
The meeting concluded with Ato Forson emphasizing the importance of international cooperation in achieving sustainable development.
“Canada’s support in agricultural modernization and resource management will complement our domestic efforts to stabilize the economy and achieve food security,” he remarked.
Both parties pledged to deepen bilateral ties to foster mutual growth and resilience.

Selon
le Programme alimentaire mondial des Nations Unies (Pam), l’Afrique de l’Ouest
et centrale seraient au bord d’une catastrophe humanitaire. La combinaison de
conflits persistants, de déplacements massifs, d’une inflation incontrôlée et
de phénomènes climatiques extrêmes pousse des millions de personnes vers la
faim aiguë. Plus de 36 millions de personnes peinent actuellement à se nourrir
dans la région. Ce chiffre pourrait grimper à plus de 52 millions durant la
période de soudure de juin à août 2025. Pour venir en aide aux personnes les
plus vulnérables, durant les trois prochains mois, le Pam a besoin de 700
millions de dollars.
Intervenant
depuis Dakar (Sénégal) durant le briefing hebdomadaire organisé par le Service
de l’Information des Nations Unies à Genève (Suisse), Sib Ollo, conseiller
régional principal pour la recherche, l’évaluation et le suivi au Pam, confirme
la gravité de la situation au Sahel en déclarant:«La situation alimentaire au
Sahel reste dramatique. Nous avons visité des communautés qui font face à des
sécheresses sans précédent dans certaines zones, et à des inondations dans
d’autres, provoquant des pertes massives de cultures et de bétail. »
Dans
le bassin du lac Tchad, des millions d’agriculteurs redoutent de ne pas pouvoir
couvrir leurs besoins alimentaires les plus élémentaires. Dans la région de
Ménaka, au Mali, des conditions de famine sont déjà signalées. L’inflation
aggrave la situation car en 2025, les prix des denrées alimentaires ont bondi
de 50 % par rapport à la moyenne des cinq dernières années. A titre d’exemple,
Sib Ollo  explique que « vendre une
chèvre aujourd’hui ne suffit même plus à acheter un demi-sac de mil ». «
Partout, nous entendons les mêmes récits déchirants. Le moment d’agir, c’est
maintenant ! »
Plus
de 10 millions de personnes ont été déplacées dans la région, dont 2,4 millions
de réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile au Tchad, Cameroun, Mauritanie et Niger. Près
de huit millions de déplacés internes, surtout au Nigeria et au Cameroun, ont
été coupés de leurs moyens de subsistance. Dans le nord du Ghana, des
agriculteurs ont dû replanter plusieurs fois leurs cultures, faute de
précipitations adéquates. À l’inverse, au nord du Nigeria, des zones comme
Jere, Mafa et Konduga ont subi des inondations destructrices. En 2024, plus de
six millions de personnes ont été affectées par les inondations dans la région.
Réponse humanitaire à bout de souffle
Malgré
l’ampleur de la crise, seulement 40 % du plan de réponse humanitaire est
actuellement financé. Le Pam a besoin d’urgence de 700 millions de dollars
américains pour venir en aide à cinq millions de personnes au cours des trois
prochains mois. « Les activités vitales doivent passer en priorité. Il faut un
investissement massif pour augmenter l’échelle des opérations », insiste Sib
Ollo. Le Service aérien humanitaire des Nations Unies (Unhas), géré par le Pam,
risque également de voir ses activités suspendues au Mali et au Nigeria faute
de financements suffisants. Ce service est pourtant indispensable pour
acheminer l’aide humanitaire dans les zones les plus isolées.
Un
instrument de coordination humanitaire a été mis en place pour rassembler les
différents acteurs face à cette crise. Mais sans engagements financiers
solides, l’impact restera limité.
Au-delà
de l’urgence, le Pam appelle à un changement structurel. Depuis 2018, son
programme intégré de résilience a permis de réhabiliter plus de 300
000 hectares de terres et d’aider quatre millions de personnes dans 3 400
villages du Sahel. Mais ces efforts ne pourront suffire sans une mobilisation
collective et durable.
Catherine Fiankan-Bokonga
a6332.en:
La Nation Benin...
According to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), West and Central Africa are on the brink of a humanitarian catastrophe. The combination of persistent conflicts, mass displacement, uncontrolled inflation and extreme climate phenomena is pushing millions of people towards acute hunger. More than 36 million people are currently struggling to feed themselves in the region. That figure could climb to more than 52 million during the lean season from June to August 2025. To assist the most vulnerable people over the next three months, WFP needs 700 million dollars.
Speaking from Dakar (Senegal) during the weekly briefing organised by the United Nations Information Service in Geneva (Switzerland), Sib Ollo, senior regional adviser for research, assessment and monitoring at WFP, confirmed the gravity of the situation in the Sahel, declaring: “The food situation in the Sahel remains dramatic. We have visited communities facing unprecedented droughts in some areas, and floods in others, causing massive losses of crops and livestock.”
In the Lake Chad basin, millions of farmers fear they will not be able to cover their most basic food needs. In the Menaka region of Mali, famine conditions are already being reported. Inflation is aggravating the situation because in 2025 food prices jumped by 50% compared with the average of the last five years. By way of example, Sib Ollo explains that “selling a goat today is no longer even enough to buy half a sack of millet.” “Everywhere, we hear the same heartbreaking accounts. The time to act is now!”
More than 10 million people have been displaced in the region, including 2.4 million refugees and asylum seekers in Chad, Cameroon, Mauritania and Niger. Nearly eight million internally displaced people, especially in Nigeria and Cameroon, have been cut off from their livelihoods. In northern Ghana, farmers have had to replant their crops several times for lack of adequate rainfall. Conversely, in northern Nigeria, areas such as Jere, Mafa and Konduga have suffered destructive floods. In 2024, more than six million people were affected by floods in the region.
A humanitarian response running out of breath
Despite the scale of the crisis, only 40% of the humanitarian response plan is currently funded. WFP urgently needs 700 million US dollars to assist five million people over the next three months. “Life-saving activities must take priority. A massive investment is needed to scale up operations,” insists Sib Ollo. The United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS), managed by WFP, also risks having its activities suspended in Mali and Nigeria for lack of sufficient funding. Yet that service is indispensable for delivering humanitarian aid to the most isolated areas.
A humanitarian coordination instrument has been set up to bring together the various actors facing this crisis. But without solid financial commitments, the impact will remain limited.
Beyond the emergency, WFP is calling for structural change. Since 2018, its integrated resilience programme has made it possible to rehabilitate more than 300,000 hectares of land and to help four million people in 3,400 villages of the Sahel. But these efforts will not suffice without collective and sustained mobilisation.
Catherine Fiankan-Bokonga

Dans l'article intitulé «Pour obtenir l’extradition de Talon : Yayi serait prêt à «brader» coton, Pvi, télécoms et chemins de fer à Bolloré» et paru dans votre journal du lundi dernier, nous parlons des coulisses de la visite du Pdg du groupe Vincent Bolloré au port.
Un accord aurait été conclu pour obtenir l’extradition de Talon. Mais selon les autorités portuaires, Vincent Bolloré est venu au port uniquement pour voir l’évolution des travaux de constructions de quais et de terminaux que son groupe construit au port.
Il y a quelques jours, Vincent Bolloré a effectué une visite de travail au Bénin au cours de laquelle il a visité les travaux financés par son groupe au port de Cotonou. On l’a vu en compagnie du Chef de l’Etat qui l’adulait et le sollicitait pour investir dans beaucoup d’autres projets au Bénin. L’hôte du Chef de l’Etat mettait l’accent, lui, sur l’importance du volet financier et les avantages que le port de Cotonou pourra tirer dès les années à venir de ce financement qui va propulser notre port dans le rang des ports modernes du monde. Selon le Chef du service communication du port, la visite de Vincent Bolloré fait partie des visites de routine qu’il organise au Bénin pour s’enquérir de l’évolution des travaux. Actuellement, le port attend d’autres investissements du second compact du Mcc et il urge que les autres soient vite achevés. «Au port avec Vincent Bolloré, on n’a pas parlé d’arrestation ou d’extradition de Patrice Talon et nous pensons qu’ailleurs (la Marina), il n’en a pas été question», souligne-t-il. Ajoutant que l’actuel Directeur général du Port autonome de Cotonou, Kassim Traoré, est très préoccupé par la résolution des urgences sur la plate forme portuaire et partage comme le Chef de l’Etat le rêve de faire de ce port un des plus modernes et des plus grands de la sous région, afin de répondre aux exigences d’une clientèle de plus en plus croissante. Dans cet article, on affirmait que «Bolloré n’est pas un philanthrope et en retour, il doit s’attendre à quelque chose. Dans les coulisses, on apprend que Boni Yayi aurait promis le Pvi, les chemins de fer et Bénin Télécoms à Vincent Bolloré. En retour, ce dernier devrait aider le gouvernement dans sa volonté obsessionnelle d’arrêter Talon». Au port, les autorités restent dubitatives et croient que Vincent Bolloré a fait une visite purement professionnelle qui n’a nullement dépassé le cadre des investissements de son groupe.
a6788.en:
Following our article on Bolloré's visit to the port: the port authorities react

In the article entitled "To obtain Talon's extradition: Yayi would be ready to 'sell off' cotton, PVI, telecoms and railways to Bolloré", published in your newspaper last Monday, we discussed the behind-the-scenes aspects of the visit by the CEO of the Vincent Bolloré group to the port.

An agreement was said to have been concluded to obtain Talon's extradition. But according to the port authorities, Vincent Bolloré came to the port solely to see the progress of the quay and terminal construction works that his group is building at the port.

A few days ago, Vincent Bolloré made a working visit to Benin during which he visited the works financed by his group at the port of Cotonou. He was seen in the company of the Head of State, who fawned over him and urged him to invest in many other projects in Benin. The Head of State's guest, for his part, emphasised the importance of the financial component and the advantages that the port of Cotonou will be able to draw in the coming years from this financing, which will propel our port into the ranks of the modern ports of the world. According to the head of the port's communication service, Vincent Bolloré's visit is one of the routine visits he makes to Benin to inquire about the progress of the works. At present, the port is awaiting further investment from the second MCC compact, and it is urgent that the others be completed quickly. "At the port with Vincent Bolloré, there was no talk of the arrest or extradition of Patrice Talon, and we think that elsewhere (the Marina) it was not discussed either," he stresses. He adds that the current Director General of the Autonomous Port of Cotonou, Kassim Traoré, is very preoccupied with resolving the urgent matters on the port platform and shares, like the Head of State, the dream of making this port one of the most modern and largest in the sub-region, in order to meet the demands of an ever-growing clientele. In that article, it was asserted that "Bolloré is not a philanthropist and in return he must expect something. Behind the scenes, we learn that Boni Yayi is said to have promised the PVI, the railways and Bénin Télécoms to Vincent Bolloré. In return, the latter was to help the government in its obsessive desire to arrest Talon." At the port, the authorities remain doubtful and believe that Vincent Bolloré made a purely professional visit that in no way went beyond the framework of his group's investments.

a6795.t:
BLOG
Amateur theatrics: An insult to Africa
By Rosa Whitaker as run in THE HILL (Congress Blog)
The Hill Amateur theatrics: An insult to Africa: Last week, I watched with dismay as two American diplomats w… https://t.co/LEkcL9Fu9K
— Congress Blog (@congressblog) May 19, 2016
******************************************
Last week, I watched with dismay as two American diplomats walked out on the inaugural address of a respected African leader who continues to make a major contribution to our shared objectives in the region and who has been a steadfast ally in the battle against global jihadism. Other African leaders attending the ceremony were visibly angered. To see two decades of goodwill built up under Presidents Bill Clinton and George Bush so carelessly forfeited was deeply saddening. Having worked for years in both administrations and the Congress to build a strong American partnership with Africa this unprecedented walk-out was personal.
The behavior of our officials reeked of arrogance. It served no US interest and advanced no conceivable strategic goal. America pays for such gratuitous grandstanding with loss of influence in Africa and in multilateral institutions where we need African support.
The target of our diplomats’ abuse was Uganda’s President Yoweri Museveni. He was being sworn in following his reelection. Although his defeated rivals have challenged the result, his share of the vote as officially tallied — 61 per cent — was entirely in line with what independent polls indicated. This was not a stolen election.
The chairman of the African Union and 14 other African heads of state were present at the swearing-in. Representing the US were deputy assistant secretary of state, Bruce Wharton, and our recently installed ambassador to Kampala, Deborah Malac. Their theatrics, leaders told me, were an insult not just to President Museveni but to all of Africa. The Russian and Chinese delegations were gleeful.
Wharton and Malac gave two reasons for their walk-out: the presence of Sudan’s President Omar al-Bashir and President Museveni’s reference to the International Criminal Court as “a bunch of useless people”. Why did the US follow the EU in this embarrassing walk-out? We followed the EU into Libya, the result — an expanded ISIL.
America needs internationalists like these who know how to disagree respectfully and secure change through engagement and persuasive argument, as opposed to amateur theatrics.
America’s attitude to the Court is hypocritical. We refused to sign the treaty that established it out of a legitimate concern it would be used against our own people. When I was in government, I had explicit instructions to lobby African countries not to sign. Since when did homage to this Court, whose jurisdiction we reject, become American policy?
In the case of Bashir, we should remember lessons learned in Iraq, Syria and Libya, ousting incumbent leaders, however unlovely, doesn’t inevitably mean change for the better. The unintended consequences have been dire.
Ugandans largely voted for peace and stability, which their government under Museveni has delivered. Predictably, the State Department was peeved by the home arrest of the opposition’s flagbearer. However, his verbal threats to overthrow an elected government through violence would also not be tolerated in the US or any country. A joke about arms at US airports warrants arrest as does a false claim of fire in a movie theater.
What makes the churlishness of our diplomats especially disgraceful is the contempt it shows for the support President Museveni is giving us — and the rest of the international community — to see that Somalia does not become another province of ISIL. Ugandan troops are fighting and dying to stop our enemies from achieving yet another haven from which to attack us.
As saddened as I am by the poor judgement exhibited by the two diplomats, I take comfort knowing that wisdom still prevails elsewhere in Washington, not least on Capitol Hill where the leadership on African issues is particularly strong at the moment on a bipartisan basis. There is not space to mention everyone, but on the House side, I would single out International Affairs Committee chairman Ed Royce and Congressmembers Charlie Rangel and Karen Bass; in the other chamber, Senators Chris Koons, Johnny Isakson and Jeff Flake.
America needs internationalists like these who know how to disagree respectfully and secure change through engagement and persuasive argument, as opposed to amateur theatrics.
********
Rosa Whitaker served as Assistant US Trade Representative for Africa in the Administrations of Bill Clinton and George W. Bush and was also a career diplomat with the State Department.

Le Burundi a abrité, le jeudi 31 octobre 2024, le 23e Sommet des chefs d’Etat et de gouvernement des pays membres du Comesa (Marché commun de l’Afrique orientale et australe) regroupant vingt-trois pays. Cette session a été l’occasion de remise et reprise entre les chefs d’Etat sortant, le Zambien Hakainde Hichilema, entrant le Burundais Evariste Ndayishimiye. Pour favoriser l’intégration, M.Ndayishimiye a indiqué que le Burundi supprime les visas de court séjour pour les pays membres du Comesa.
Lors de cette session, le chef de l’Etat burundais, Evariste Ndayishimiye a d’abord souhaité la bienvenue à ses homologues qui ont rehaussé de leur présence ces assises, les Premiers ministres, les parlementaires et autres délégations. Il a ainsi souligné que le Burundi est le carrefour, l’intersection de différentes communautés sur le continent tout en indiquant que le Burundi est une plaque tournante, une plate-forme d’un vaste marché régional.
Le président Ndayishimiye a ainsi manifesté sa joie d’avoir reçu ses homologues et autres délégations pour échanger sur les sujets qui tiennent à cœur la région du Comesa. «Le Sommet est une occasion pour nous de nous évaluer et planifier ensemble les projets d’avenir de notre communauté. Cette dernière a déjà atteint la maturité, et c’est le grand moment de planifier pour améliorer les conditions de vie des populations», a-t-il fait entendre.
Le président Ndayishimiye a également mis l’accent sur le secteur agricole en indiquant que c’est le pilier de l’économie de la région. Selon toujours lui, l’agriculture est la plus grande activité pourvoyeur d’emplois dans la région, bien que menacée par le changement climatique. Il a également souligné que l’exploitation minière est aussi le lévier du développement économique de la région avant d’inclure le secteur du tourisme dans les secteurs porteurs de croissance. Le numéro Un burundais a aussi partagé aux participants l’ambition du Burundi d’aboutir à l’autosuffisance alimentaire pour aussi avoir du surplus à vendre à l’extérieur.
Promouvoir le Commerce entre les pays membres du Comesa
Dans son allocution, le Chef de l’Etat Zambien, Hakainde Hichilema, président sortant du Comesa, a présenté les réalisations de cette communauté pendant sa présidence. A cet effet, au cours de la période allant de 2020 à 2023, le commerce extra Comesa, c’est-à-dire les exportations en dehors du Comesa, a passé de 100 milliards de dollars américains à deux-cent dix-neuf milliards de dollars américains. Quant au commerce intra Comesa, les réalisations sont de dix milliards de dollars américains en 2020 à quatorze milliards de dollars américains en 2023.
Le président sortant du Comesa a insisté sur la nécessité et l’importance de promouvoir le commerce entre les pays membres du Comesa et booster les investissements. «L’Afrique nous appartient, nous devons fournir beaucoup d’efforts pour développer le commerce entre nos pays et renforcer l’intégration économique», a-t-il indiqué, tout en précisant que les résultats déjà atteints laissent à croire que l’on doit faire plus dans ce domaine.
M. Hakainde a, en effet, appelé les pays membres à tout faire pour prioriser l’intégration économique et la stabilité dans la région, tout en rappelant l’impact très négatif de l’instabilité sur la vie quotidienne, l’économie, etc dans la région.
Le Burundi supprime les visas de court séjour pour les ressortissants des pays membres du Comesa
Cette session a également été une occasion de remise et reprise entre le président sortant et celui entrant, le chef de l’Etat burundais qui va assurer la présidence du Comesa pendant une période d’une année. La vice-présidence est assurée par le président kényan. Le président entrant a, en effet, exprimé son engagement ferme d’œuvrer pour le développement du Comesa. Pour favoriser l’intégration régionale, M. Ndayishimiye a précisé que le Burundi supprime les visas de court séjour pour les ressortissants des pays membres du Comesa.
D’autres chefs d’Etat et de gouvernement ainsi que les délégations ont également eu l’occasion de s’exprimer. Dans leurs interventions, ceux qui ont pris la parole ont exprimé leurs engagements à la réalisation des objectifs du Comesa. Ainsi, ils ont mentionné certaines réalisations dans divers domaines et les perspectives de leurs pays respectifs qui apporteront une contribution pources objectifs.
Claude Hakizimana
Laurent Mpundunziza

Burundi hosted, on Thursday 31 October 2024, the 23rd Summit of Heads of State and Government of the member countries of COMESA (Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa), bringing together twenty-three countries. This session was the occasion for the handover between the outgoing Head of State, Zambian Hakainde Hichilema, and the incoming one, Burundian Evariste Ndayishimiye. To promote integration, Mr Ndayishimiye indicated that Burundi is abolishing short-stay visas for COMESA member countries.

During this session, the Burundian Head of State, Evariste Ndayishimiye, first welcomed his counterparts who honoured these proceedings with their presence, the Prime Ministers, the parliamentarians and other delegations. He thus stressed that Burundi is the crossroads, the intersection of different communities on the continent, while indicating that Burundi is a hub, a platform of a vast regional market.

President Ndayishimiye thus expressed his joy at having received his counterparts and other delegations in order to discuss the subjects that are dear to the COMESA region. "The Summit is an opportunity for us to assess ourselves and to plan together the future projects of our community. The latter has already reached maturity, and this is the great moment to plan in order to improve the living conditions of the populations," he said.

President Ndayishimiye also placed emphasis on the agricultural sector, indicating that it is the pillar of the region's economy. Again according to him, agriculture is the largest job-providing activity in the region, although it is threatened by climate change. He also stressed that mining is likewise the lever of the region's economic development, before including the tourism sector among the growth-bearing sectors. Burundi's Number One also shared with the participants Burundi's ambition to achieve food self-sufficiency so as also to have a surplus to sell abroad.

Promoting Trade among COMESA member countries

In his address, the Zambian Head of State, Hakainde Hichilema, outgoing President of COMESA, presented the achievements of this community during his presidency. In this respect, over the period from 2020 to 2023, extra-COMESA trade, that is to say exports outside COMESA, rose from 100 billion US dollars to two hundred and nineteen billion US dollars. As for intra-COMESA trade, the achievements went from ten billion US dollars in 2020 to fourteen billion US dollars in 2023.

The outgoing President of COMESA insisted on the necessity and the importance of promoting trade among COMESA member countries and of boosting investment. "Africa belongs to us, we must make great efforts to develop trade between our countries and to strengthen economic integration," he said, while specifying that the results already achieved suggest that more must be done in this area.

Mr Hakainde in fact called on the member countries to do everything to prioritize economic integration and stability in the region, while recalling the very negative impact of instability on daily life, the economy, etc. in the region.

Burundi abolishes short-stay visas for nationals of COMESA member countries

This session was also an occasion for the handover between the outgoing president and the incoming one, the Burundian Head of State, who will hold the COMESA presidency for a period of one year. The vice-presidency is held by the Kenyan president. The incoming president in fact expressed his firm commitment to work for the development of COMESA. In order to promote regional integration, Mr Ndayishimiye specified that Burundi is abolishing short-stay visas for nationals of COMESA member countries.

Other Heads of State and Government as well as the delegations also had the opportunity to speak. In their interventions, those who took the floor expressed their commitments to the achievement of COMESA's objectives. Thus, they mentioned certain achievements in various areas and the prospects of their respective countries which will make a contribution to these objectives.

Claude Hakizimana
Laurent Mpundunziza

Namibia has welcomed Cuba’s removal from the United States’ list of state sponsors of terrorism, which president Joe Biden announced in one of his final official acts.
President Nangolo Mbumba has commended Biden’s decision to remove Cuba from the list of state sponsors of terrorism.
In a media statement released yesterday, Mbumba welcomed the announcement, reaffirming Namibia’s long-standing support for Cuba.
“I commend the US government for having eventually taken the long-overdue decision to remove Cuba from the list of state sponsors of terrorism. Namibia has consistently advocated for the removal of Cuba from the list, deeming it arbitrary, unjust and with no basis in international law,” he stated.
Mbumba emphasised that while the decision marks progress, further action is still necessary to improve relations between the two nations.
“This step should be followed by tangible actions by the US government to end the unjust and illegal economic blockade against Cuba”, he urged.
Until Biden’s announcement, Cuba had been placed alongside North Korea, Syria and Iran on the US state sponsors of terrorism list, and were deemed by the US government to have repeatedly provided support for acts of international terrorism.
Inclusion on the list enables the US government to impose four main types of unilateral sanctions, which are restriction of foreign aid, a ban on weapons sales, heightened control over the export of dual-use equipment, and other miscellaneous economic sanctions.
In return for its removal, Cuba is expected to release over 553 political prisoners as
part of the new deal, which was reportedly brokered by the Catholic Church, and comes just days before president-elect Donald Trump is due to be sworn in.
“Namibia further believes that this move is expected to ease some economic restrictions and foster better understanding, as well as result in good diplomatic relations. Namibia is confident that this gesture by the outgoing US administration will contribute to strengthening international cooperation, and hopes that the incoming administration will continue to maintain the same diplomatic posture for the mutual benefit of the two countries and peoples,” said Penda Naanda, the executive director in the Ministry of International Relations and Cooperation.
He added that the latest development could pave the way for further cooperation and mutual understanding between Cuba and the US, especially in the economic and social arenas.
Solidarity
Over the years, the Namibian government has been vocal in its support for Cuba’s continued fight against the US economic, financial and commercial blockade against the island nation.
Besides having had Cuba on that list, the US has to date maintained a 60-year-old economic blockade against Cuba, which prevents American businesses from conducting trade or commerce with that nation, and has negatively impacted all sectors of the Cuban economy.
During his two-day State visit to Cuba late last year, Mbumba had labelled the ongoing blockade against Cuba as the most enduring and inhumane trade embargo in modern history.

a7465.t:
Nigeria struggles to rein in a widespread meningitis outbreak
While cases first recorded in October have spread to 23 of Nigeria’s 36 states, nearly half of the deaths, 74, were reported this year, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control said this week, with local partners describing the recent rise in fatalities as “alarming".
Most deaths from the disease have been mainly due to infected people not going to health facilities or arriving there late with severe complications, NCDC spokesperson Sani Datti told The Associated Press, a common problem in past outbreaks in the country.
The current outbreak has hit Africa’s most populous country as its health sector reels from US aid cuts ordered by the Trump administration in February that have affected multiple countries. Nigeria relied heavily on such aid over the years to help fight similar outbreaks and support its underfunded healthcare systems.
Seasonal meningitis outbreaks are common during the dry season, especially in northern Nigeria. Almost all the worst-hit states are in the north, where health providers have warned the outbreak is rapidly spreading in hard-to-reach areas.
Meningitis, more common during the hot season in Nigeria, affects the protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It’s a major public health challenge for a country already grappling with “the world’s highest burden of malaria,” according to the World Health Organisation.
Disease response
Last week, Nigeria received the first batch of more than 1 million vaccine doses from the global vaccine alliance Gavi, described by local officials as a crucial milestone in disease response.
The Nigeria CDC also said it is working with state authorities to scale up disease surveillance with a focus on tracking new cases, laboratory testing, and public sensitisation campaigns to curb the outbreak.
Campaigns are also being rolled out, urging residents to take precautionary measures and seek immediate medical attention if they are experiencing symptoms such as high fever, stiff neck and severe headaches.
However, access to hospitals remains a huge problem, local partners say.
“We have seen hundreds of admissions and scores of deaths in just a few weeks. The high fatality rate is due to access (to) care, there are challenges with that and low vaccination coverage,” said Simba Tirima, Nigeria’s country representative for French medical charity Doctors Without Borders, or MSF.
Tirima told the AP that the most vulnerable are residents in remote areas who often arrive late to MSF facilities.
“We know that meningitis progresses rapidly, and patients’ (conditions) can deteriorate in 24 hours,” he said, calling for mass vaccination campaigns.
